learningObjectives: Link a TestSheet to a Template.
Link the TestSheet Values to the TestStep Values in the Template.
Use the Check Template and Jump to Schema functions.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Linking a TestSheet to a Template

elements.text: A TestSheet or Class supplies data to the Template. The Template models the flow; a TemplateInstance contains the generated concrete tests.

elements.title: Link the TestSheet
items: Drag the TestSheet or Class onto the Template.
Inspect SchemaName to confirm the source type and name.
Plan reuse intentionally. The documentation does not impose a universal one-TestSheet/one-Template restriction; Classes can centralize shared business-data structure.

elements.text: With the Template selected, Jump to Schema Definition (Ctrl+J) navigates to its schema. SchemaName also identifies its linked TestCase-Design source.

Tosca can create XL paths automatically for empty TestStepValues whose names uniquely match source Attribute names. Inspect those generated paths. Other values need an explicit path; linking a source does not guarantee every mapping is complete.

elements.title: Link TestSheet Values to TestStepValues
items: Use the required source Attribute path for each mapped TestStepValue.
Paths such as {XL[Person.First Name]} follow the source hierarchy.
Check each created path and the intended input/assertion ActionMode.

elements.description: Check Template compares the model against its schema, including Attribute references, specified conditions, custom properties, TCPs and InstanceName. It does not prove correct business logic or successful live-SUT execution.

elements.text: A successful schema check is not an execution test. Review expected results and run the generated cases.

Manual XL paths such as {XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} are supported. Automatic mapping or drag-and-drop can reduce typing, but neither guarantees semantic correctness; inspect the source path and expected meaning.

Instantiation needs a Template, a linked data source and correctly mapped values. WorkState is inherited by generated cases; Completed is not listed as a universal prerequisite for creating the TemplateInstance.

elements.title: Instantiate
items: Create TemplateInstance from the selected Template, use Instantiate in the ribbon, or Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.
Inspect the generated cases and their intended data/conditions.
Run a small representative selection in ScratchBook before organizing formal execution.
When model or data changes, review manual edits and reinstantiate the appropriate TemplateInstance.

elements.text: For the hypothetical four-combination example, inspect the generated set rather than assuming each Attribute value becomes one test. Conditions, Break and selectors may affect the generated subset; the Template and data links remain model dependencies.

Use synthetic login combinations. Link their TestSheet, inspect each XL path, check the model and generate a TemplateInstance. Compare a representative valid and negative case with the intended assertions. Original Academy exercise instructions were inaccessible and remain unverified.

examPitfalls.title: Schema validation is broader than reference existence
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ignoring conditions and model properties, or treating a schema check as execution proof.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect Check Template findings, then separately validate actual test behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Mapping is conditional
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming all values map automatically, or that none can map automatically.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Automatic paths require empty values and unique matching names; inspect every mapping.

examPitfalls.title: Model reuse is intentional
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating one-TestSheet/one-Template as an engine restriction.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose a maintainable data model; verify the actual source attached to each Template.

examPitfalls.title: Manual paths are supported
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming typed XL paths are invalid or generated paths are always correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use supported syntax and inspect both the path and its intended meaning.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you link a TestSheet to a Template in Tosca?

options.text: TestSheets link automatically to the most recently created Template.
Right-click the Template and select 'Import TestSheet'.
Select the TestSheet in TestCaseDesign, then drag and drop it onto the Template in the TestCase section.
Copy the TestSheet's XML and paste it into the Template's properties.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a drag-and-drop action, same direction as most Tosca linking.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You select the TestSheet from TestCaseDesign and drag it onto the Template in the TestCase section to link them.

optionExplanations.A: A newly created Template is not automatically linked to the last TestSheet.
optionExplanations.B: Import TestSheet is not the documented linking operation here.
optionExplanations.C: Drop the TestSheet onto the Template to assign its source.
optionExplanations.D: Pasting XML is not the documented source-assignment workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the Check Template function actually validate?

options.text: That all formulas used in Conditions produce the correct output.
That the ExecutionList linked to the Template is configured correctly.
That every TestStep will execute correctly against the live SUT.
Schema-based references, specified conditions and relevant properties including TCPs and InstanceName; this does not guarantee live execution success.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish model validation from successful business assertions at execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Check Template considers more than existence of XL links, but it does not run every test against the SUT.

optionExplanations.A: Model checking does not establish correct business outcomes for all formulas.
optionExplanations.B: This is a Template/schema check, not complete execution-list validation.
optionExplanations.C: It does not execute every TestStep against the live system.
optionExplanations.D: The check includes schema-based conditions and properties, beyond link existence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the shortcut to jump directly from a Template to its linked TestSheet?

options.text: Ctrl+J (Jump to Schema Definition).
Ctrl+T.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.

practiceQuiz.hint: Not the same shortcut as Instantiate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+J is the shortcut for 'Jump to Schema Definition', which navigates from the Template directly to its linked TestSheet. Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I is the Instantiate shortcut, not this one.

optionExplanations.A: F9 toggles visibility in the active context.
optionExplanations.B: With the Template selected this command jumps to its schema definition.
optionExplanations.C: Ctrl+T searches and adds a TestStep.
optionExplanations.D: This chord creates a TemplateInstance rather than navigating the schema.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which description correctly explains XL mapping when linking a TestSheet to a Template?

options.text: Empty TestStepValues with uniquely matching Attribute names can get automatic XL paths; inspect them and explicitly map the remaining values.
Type the value's name manually into the TestStepValue field.
XL references cannot be created manually; only Instantiate creates them.
Use the Check Template function to auto-link all values.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same drag-and-drop pattern as linking the TestSheet itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Automatic mapping has specific conditions. Manually specified paths are also supported; Check Template does not supply every missing mapping.

optionExplanations.A: The documented automatic mapping conditions are empty values and unique matching names.
optionExplanations.B: A bare name alone is not the XL expression for a data path.
optionExplanations.C: Manual paths are supported; instantiation is not their only creation mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: Checking validates the model rather than guaranteeing all missing values are mapped.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are valid ways to Instantiate a Template?

options.text: Right-click the Template → Create TemplateInstance from the Mini Toolbar.
Select the Template and use the shortcut Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I.
Rename the Template to 'Instance_1'.
Select the Template, click Instantiate in the Ribbon's TestCase tab.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is a ribbon button, one is a context menu action, one is a keyboard shortcut.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instantiation can be triggered via the Ribbon's Instantiate button, via right-click → Create TemplateInstance, or via the Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I shortcut. Renaming does nothing functionally. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: The context command creates the TemplateInstance from the selected model.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented creation/instantiation chord.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming does not generate concrete cases.
optionExplanations.D: Instantiate is also available through the TestCases ribbon.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TestCase-Design structure can centralize reusable business-data definitions across different TestSheets?

options.text: Classes.
Multiple copies of the same TestSheet, pasted into each Template.
RequirementSets.
ExecutionLists.

practiceQuiz.hint: Choose a reusable data-design structure rather than an execution or risk container.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Classes centralize reusable data structure; this is separate from an unsupported claim that a TestSheet can only ever feed one Template.

optionExplanations.A: Classes model reusable data definitions for different design structures.
optionExplanations.B: Copies create separate definitions and increase duplicated maintenance.
optionExplanations.C: RequirementSets organize risk/coverage rather than this reusable data structure.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionLists organize test runs rather than shared data definitions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the manual syntax for typing an XL reference directly into a TestStepValue, and is it recommended?

options.text: $XL{Attribute::SubAttribute}$ — valid and equally recommended as drag-and-drop.
{XL[Attribute.SubAttribute]} is supported; inspect its source hierarchy and intended meaning, whether typed or generated.
There is no manual syntax; XL references can only ever be created by drag-and-drop.
{CP[Attribute.SubAttribute]} — the recommended and only supported method.

practiceQuiz.hint: Don't confuse this with the {CP[...]} syntax used for Test Configuration Parameters.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dot-separated Attribute levels within an XL expression are supported. Typing is valid, and generated paths also require inspection.

optionExplanations.A: This is not supported XL data-path syntax.
optionExplanations.B: XL with dot-separated levels is supported; inspect its hierarchy and meaning.
optionExplanations.C: Typed paths are supported, so drag-and-drop is not the sole method.
optionExplanations.D: CP recalls a configuration parameter, not the TestSheet Attribute path.

quickRecap.value: Drop a TestSheet or Class on the Template and inspect SchemaName.
Requires empty values with uniquely matching Attribute names; inspect all paths.
Check Template includes schema references, conditions and relevant properties, not live execution proof.
Create TemplateInstance, inspect and trial-run; model changes require reinstantiation.
